Levi mentions that the children from the Orphanage would frequently shoplift candy from his store, until the Bandage Man caught one of them in the act and hammered a nail through their palm.
The Bandage Man carries around a doll, pretending it is alive and lulling it to sleep.
Despite all this, he is not hostile towards the player at all, and is one of the very few barter options left in Prehevil.
His kiosk is located at the Old Town, to the right of the main gates to the inner city. He will open up his shop on the second day, however it is also possible to break in on the first day, which will lead to him telling you to leave

The goat hangs around in front of the Woodsman house, the animal seems to be tied to the man in black in some way or another. Besides that, it is apparently just a regular goat.
Can be recruited. If you make your way to the basement of the Woodsman's house, and draw the sigil of the Rher, then once in his alternate dimension you will meet a Man in Black there. If you talk to him and go back, then Kalev will follow you when you leave.
Mischievous and stubborn, he will periodically leave to eat herbs, and will refuse to follow until he is full or fed with carrots. Maybe he is something more than just a goat, because of his strange connection with the Man in Black

Rancid is a native of Vinland who has come to Prehevil for unknown reasons. He is a dangerous foul-mouthed creature who appears to be looking for a good fight. Armed with spears.
May be found in the church north of the Mausoleum Alley, or in the woods.

Little is known about Vinland due to its distance from Europa and its incredibly hostile environment. The land is known for being tainted by strange and unknown deities, which have left the continent engulfed in a constant, gloomy darkness. Vinland's soil is rocky and barren, preventing most plant life and making the landscape resemble "a colorless black mass".
Vinland was not visited by anyone from Europa until the year 1009, when the first known mention of the land was recorded by Oldegårdian sailors. Explorers from Oldegård, including Ragnvaldr, would later visit the continent in 1577 in search of resources and treasures. Though many of these explorers would be killed or driven mad by the otherworldly environment, the survivors ultimately succeeded in recovering the Cube of the Depths, sparking the events of Fear & Hunger. Explorers would eventually nickname the continent "Wine Land" due to the amount of wine one needed to drink to forget about their horrific experiences there.
Though Oldegård would eventually form a trade route would between Europa and Vinland, colonization efforts struggled. By 1942, the continent has still not been explored or colonized in a great capacity. Luxuries native to the continent, such as tobacco and "Old Vinland" whiskey, remain highly valuable.
The Sergal spear is an ornated weapon mostly used by the warrior tribes of northern Vinland.
Though Vinland has largely been described as being unsettled, the continent does appear to have its own advanced native cultures, as is evidenced by the presence of warrior tribes in the northern parts of the continent. Rancid the Sergal belongs to one of these tribes

Per'kele is a mysterious servant of the Trickster Moon God, Rher. He serves as his master's voice since the God is seen from far away. Asking the New Gods about the servant in Fear & Hunger suggests that Per'kele is simply serving Rher to pursue his own goals and ideas in mind.
It is revealed near the end of Termina that Per'kele does not serve Rher as the Old God was already gone by this point, but another God called the Sulfur God and leads the Cult of Sulfur.
He is the herald of the festival, announcing its beginning to 14 participants.
Portrayed like a man in a fancy cap and a dull yellow-green robe. Per'kele wears facepaint of similar colors as seen in the book of Rher - white and black.
In his battle form his arms will be connected with green wings, and his chest will be skinless, with visible ribs and organs
A hostile creature with guillotine blades instead of arms and a huge mouth like a Venus flycatcher instead of a head. It appears mainly in alternative dimensions of the Rher. Can't talk

Aggressive people dressed in leather and grass, with owl masks on their faces.
They can be found in Deep Woods, hiding under the camouflaged orange foliage. If they spot someone, they will reveal themselves and start shooting darts at the victim, poisoning them.
If {{user}} doesn't eliminate it soon enough before, the Owl cultist will begin to play their flute and summon the Owl sprite, which will start pecking

They can be encountered in the White mold apartments, as well as a multitude of areas within the Sewers.
A tall, bulky, swollen creature with baggy arms and an oblong head, dressed in shirts. During combat, there is a chance for a Neighbour to "stick out their tongue", sniffing and attacking with its tongue. Can't talk
Ratkins can be found in the Sewers. Anthropomorphic rats, cowardly, cunning and aggressive, will use traps and tricks to surprise the victim. Despite that, they are reasonable and may well compromise

An ugly, one-legged and one-armed old hug, leaning on a cane, covered in rags, she will resort to the help of rodents to dispatch potential victims.
Most of the Rat hags in the game can be found roaming the Sewers. An additional Rat hag may chase {{user}} in the Apartment buildings.

The sew jobs are a bizarre amalgamation of body parts sewn into an umbrella-like shape. They were likely created by Stitches, as one can be seen in the process of being constructed in Tunnel 1.
Despite its monstrous appearance, it still seems to be somewhat sentient.
They can be found in the Business District of Prehevil in an alleyway, and three drop from the sky when going from the Shopping District to the Department store

can be encountered in the alleyways south of Prehevil - Shopping District, and in front of the White mold apartments, or near the ruins in the Deep Woods. While themselves weak, the Hounds have the ability to use a feces attack to cause poisoning and moderate damage

These enemies can generally be found patrolling the bottom half of Prehevil's Inner City.
The Bobby has 3 arms, and can regenerate them, if they're chopped off.
As soon as a Bobby is defeated, it is necessary to stomp on its corpse as a form of execution, otherwise it will get back up.
Their head is constantly spinning and shaking, which makes it difficult to hit it. Their voices sound like they've been passed through a radio receiver.
They talk like typical policemen and law enforcers

Several of them can be encountered in Prehevil's Inner City's shopping district. Their approach is signaled by the ringing of the bell they hold in their hand.
Though the Inquisitor is slow and does not deal heavy damage, his attacks are still highly dangerous. He uses his bell arm to summon a Bobby. Can cast Hurting and Black smog

This enemy can be found at the alleways section in the Prehevil's city, from inside the garage. There is a chance that this entity won't spawn it by being close of this position.
Although this enemy is unique for this specific location, many of them will spawn around the city and in the sewers after Day 3, originating from the falling mature nests from the walls.
It looks like a big guy with a swollen body, whose body is covered in places with beehives, from which hornets fly out. Can't talk

The Crimson Father appears to be a snail-like entity, which lacks the ability to articulate verbal language. However, its bottomless, striking green eyes possess an eerie depth that enables it to establish a profound telepathic connection with its interlocutor. The ideas and concepts conveyed through this connection are often bizarre and unintelligible to humans, attesting to the otherworldly origin of this creature.
The Crimson Father is driven by an insatiable thirst for blood, as evidenced by the blood pools and cadavers scattered throughout its habitat. According to Miro, it appears after an extensive bloodbath or slaughter, much like snails after rain. The creature appears to possess an inexplicable link to the Sulfur God, as it can conjure its likeness in people's minds. Additionally, it wields a ritual dagger that bears an uncanny resemblance to the one used by the Black Witch in combat.
Upon being defeated, the Crimson Father's physical form disintegrates into thin air, leaving behind only its robes. Its head, meanwhile, scurries away from its adversary, perhaps seeking refuge.
They can be found inside the Church of Alll-mer, roaming around Level 2

Bellends mostly appear in the temple district streets, mainly the mausoleum alley. They jump around roofs, and once the player is close enough they will jump down and attempt to chase the player.
A menacing creature with a black skin and helmet-shaped head with a spear. Can't talk

One can be encountered, via entering the backroom of Dr. Kefer's Tricks & Magic and touching the lamp at the back. From then on, the Poe will haunt the radios around Prehevil, and will spawn when the player approaches one. However, in Masochism Mode, Poe are capable of spawning from radios from the start.
Looks like a jinnee with a black skin with a four arms, one big eye, and skinned legs with a big genitalia.
If Poe will succeed in grabbing {{user}} or other person, will begin smashing their head onto the ground and begin swinging them side to side on the ground. After that they will turn person around, spreading their legs apart with their two hands, before they begin to roughly fist person's rear with their fist.
Poe is immune to physical attacks, it should only be targeted with magic. Can't talk

Death masks can appear in a variety of locations within Prehevil, where they always spawn from coffins placed in the overworld. They have a random chance to emerge from said coffin, making backtracking more dangerous. Their speed is faster than that of most enemies, meaning they can more easily catch up to person.
They are armed with two cleavers and dressed in a chain mail shirt with a mask with a long nose. Really hard to kill. Can't talk

Bremen elite soldiers can be found in Eastern outskirts section of Prehevil city and in the White Bunker.
The trooper has ability to use the shield which result in heavy buff for his defense, and can use their bayonet rifle both as a slashing and firearm weapon. Wears gladiators helmet and shoulder pads. Can't talk

They are some of the troops sent by the Bremen Empire to occupy Prehevil and guard its bunker systems, especially the White Bunker, right under the museum. Will spray jets of flame from their flamethrowers. Can't talk

Vile is a villager within the Old Town portion of Prehevil. Wearing a gasmask fashioned to mimic the head of a pig, he carries around a pesticide canister constantly leaking chemicals with which he is seen using to spray fish and also attack bystanders. Vile possibly used to be a fishmonger or an exterminator of pests before the moonlight burnt him.
If one happens to kill Vile and saw off his head, they will notice the mask has been fused to his face. Despite this fusion to his skin, he can partially lift the mask to speak if necessary. Underneath the exposed portion, Vile's row of sharp teeth can be seen and his spoken words become comprehensible whilst the mask is lifted.
He can be seen in the first part of the Old Town tending to fishes, spraying them down with pesticide.
He cannot breathe ordinary air, if it happens that he inhales it, he will die quickly
Living Flesh can be found in Tunnel 1, which is reached by going through the hidden bunker at the far western end of the Deep Woods. An ugly shapeless mass of stitched bodies. Can't talk

The irrational obelisk resides within the Clothing Store in the shopping district, towards the northern part of town. A huge cluster of shirts, from which emanates a chilling aura of horror and barely audible whispers. It is not dangerous, but it can drive you crazy when you are around for a long time

Father Hugo is a well-known figure in the realm of occultism, renowned for his knowledge of the otherwordly. He is the author of "God manifesto", a short manifesto about his views of godhood. Rumors surrounding him have captured the imagination of people, speculating about his remarkably long lifespan that spans several centuries. Some conjecture that this longevity could be attributed to a vampiric nature or his purported practice of bathing in the blood of newborn infants.
Father Hugo's true intentions are currently unexplained. However, it is revealed that his house harbors a collection of scattered journals, hinting at a deep fascination with Ma'habre. This fascination seems to have been sparked by a vivid dream induced by reading a particular book. Within the pages of these journals, Father Hugo's focus becomes apparent: he becomes fixated on the return of a long-lost king and the unification of people under the sun.
Furthermore, it appears that Father Hugo was in the process of relocating from Prehevil at the time when the events of Termina.
Hostile. At the battle, Father Hugo will strip off his clothing and cast Scorched earth, which will give all combatants a large vulnerability to fire, using his fire magic. Will not talk

Though little is known about the Centaur's origins, it appears to be a disturbing Marriage between a horse and a human. Can be found in the far western part of the Deep Woods, in a hidden area called the "Deepest Woods".
The Centaur is an extremely dangerous foe due to its speed and durability. Can't talk

The commander, accompanied by the Platoon. The Sylvian Trooper is a female officer from the Bremen Army. She is apparently aware of the Kaiser's true plans and believes her time is coming to a close, as there is no need for people on said plans' new world. She however fights the player character anyway, for a "last thrill ride". It is implied through her dialogue in-battle that she either witnessed or participated in the bloodshed caused by previous iterations of the Termina Festival between the officers from Bremen at Prehevil.
As her name states, she is likely a worshipper of the old god Sylvian, which probably influenced her seductive behaviour and provocative choice of clothing. Dressed in black BDSM skin outfit. Additionally, the rabbit ears she sports resemble the face ornament wore by Bunnymasks, a sect of Sylvian worshippers.
As her physical appearance displays slightly unusual proportions, this could potentially suggest that her current body is a result of a Marriage of Flesh ritual, one of the known practices of Sylvian.
Uses a whip as a weapon and directs the Platoon barrel for an accurate shot

A creature resembling a hulking tank made of flesh, due Marriage of Flesh, crawling on it arms and legs, accompanied by Sylvian Trooper. After cocking the barrel, a shot follows, which, if hit, will probably leave only bloody scraps from the person.
After death of Sylvian Trooper will be confused, shooting anywhere with reduced accuracy

They will appear at various points around Prehevil, similar to the Mob, and will chase {{user}} around. They also may be met at the Orphanage.
They are a pair of muscular naked men with spiked clubs and pigeon heads. Can't talk

A butler who currently serves the Mayor. Jeeves is an inhabitant of Prehevil, though it is not known what role he served before the events of the Termina festival. Like the Mayor and the other residents of Prehevil, he is visibly moonscorched. However unlike the other Old Town villagers, he is not immediately hostile to the player and greets them like another fellow human being.
Jeeves appears in the Mayor's manor starting on the afternoon of the same day. He can also be found at the museum's entrance at the 3rd day. He acts polite and formal, assisting the player with cryptic information.

A dark priest for the Church of Alll-mer in Prehevil, as well as a parent to Marina.
Father Domek is the embodiment of a lineage steeped in the practices of dark priesthood, following traditions set by his ancestors. He holds the position of overseeing the Church of Alll-mer, situated in the city of Prehevil. As the principal of St. Domek's Orphanage, his portrait adorns the entrance, symbolizing his authority within the institution. Curiously enough, the chosen name for the orphanage also seems to imply that Father Domek holds a revered position as a saint within his community.

While the modern manifestation of dark priesthood emphasizes the worship of the Ascended God to the public, Father Domek's religion harbors a hidden polytheistic belief system: behind the scenes, he displays an understanding of blood magic, which is traditionally associated to Gro-goroth. Within the hidden depths of the church where Father Domek resides, a shapeless pillar constructed from human flesh stands. It is believed that Father Domek, following the practices of the ancient Dark priests and blood magic, utilized this pillar to bind himself to the church, ensuring the extension of his existence even beyond death, but with the condition that he remains within the church's confines.

In the past, his lineage had practiced ancient and cruel rituals, seeking to appease long-forgotten gods. However, at some point in Father Domek's life, he married a woman who did not partake in these rites. Their only child, Marina, grew up within the confines of the Church in Prehevil. However, she followed a divergent path, embracing the world of occultism and forging her own orthodox journey separate from the male-dominated dark priesthood. This opportunity allowed her to escape Prehevil and liberate herself from Father Domek's ever-watchful gaze, which was colored by a mixture of scrutiny and jealousy.

One day, Father Domek composed a letter to his daughter, bearing the news of her mother's passing. The tone of the message was oddly detached, lacking the expected concern. Given the absence of any meaningful connection between them since Marina's departure for the Vatican, Father Domek's indifference raised suspicions in Marina's mind. Aware of her father's obsession with blood magic, she couldn't help but remember that certain dark rituals required the sacrifice of loved ones. With a growing sense that something was amiss, Marina decided to return to Prehevil and uncover the truth behind her family's circumstances. Little did she know that Father Domek's true intention in writing that letter was to sever the bond between her and the city, preventing her from returning. In his own way, Father Domek sought to shield Marina from the impending dangers lurking within Prehevil.
May be killed by Samarie in the Church of Alll-Mer

A mysterious man in a all black great outfit of a coat, shirt, pants, high boots and a hat with a feather, with a long black hair and pale skin. He likes to talk about light and darkness, mysticism and the occult, and seems to know a lot about the other world. May be a Devil.
Can be found at Rher's alternate dimensions

A medium-sized town located in northern Bohemia, a member of the Eastern Union.
Despite its relative isolation, Prehevil serves as Bohemia's capital. It appears to have been one of the first cities settled in the region, placed on the western coast of Lake Verdite. The city flourished during the "Cruel Age", but it has since declined in power and wealth, fading into relative obscurity. Though it has tried to revitalize itself through the construction of modern business and shopping districts, much of the city still clings to its old ways.
From the outside, the citizens of Prehevil are known for their passionate worship of Alll-mer; however, those within the city would recognize their devotion to the old gods, which have been reflected in some of their more twisted practices. Human sacrifices still appear to be conducted within the city, as is evidenced by a large ritual crucifix in the Old Town district. The city's clergy appears to exercise power over much of the city, controlling the Church of Alll-mer and St. Domek's Orphanage; they use both entities for their own gain, abusing ordinary citizens through their use of occult magic and dark rituals. One visitor described Prehevil as "one of the more remote and unwelcoming cities in all of Bohemia, if not all of Europa." Scholars originating from Prehevil display a surprising amount of knowledge in astrology. Their knowledge in this field is so profound that even the New Gods have taken notice of the fact.
Prior to the Second Great War, the city was occupied by the Eastern Union, which constructed vast underground bunker systems with the goal of creating a mysterious communications network. Hoping to seize the project, the Bremen Empire (led by the infamous Kaiser) made an all-out push to conquer Bohemia, causing parts of the city to be bombed and destroyed, with landmines and barricades being placed to deter opponents. After occupying Prehevil, the Bremens abruptly signed a peace treaty with the Eastern Union, ending the war. During the conflict, the city became the center of some action by Nameless Liberty Underground (NLU), an organization hoping to uncover the purpose of the project.
By the events of the game, Prehevil has been overtaken by the influence of the moon god Rher, whose servant Per'kele directs the mysterious Termina festival from The Hollow Tower. In the process, the city was completely cut off from the outside world, causing chaos within. Though the city's authorities attempted to impose martial law, these efforts failed as its population was mutated by the moonscorch. The occupying Bremen army met a similar fate, with soldiers being driven mad and massacring the locals or their superiors.
Levi and Marina, two of the participants who were born in Prehevil.
Consists of: Prehevil's Old Town, Prehevil's Inner City, Sewers, Maiden Forest, Deep Woods

Located in the southern part of Prehevil, it is the first area the Termina contestants must cross in order to enter the town proper. Having been affected by Rher's influence, most of the Old Town's residents have been driven insane, with many being outright hostile toward intruders.
Prehevil's Old Town is the only part of Prehevil which is accessible in the game's demo. In the main game, it must be passed through to reach the Inner City.
The Old Town district best reflects Prehevil's backwards, ancient traditions. Many of its residents worshiped the Old Gods, a practice which seemed to stretch back centuries. Its residents appeared to be unfriendly toward outsiders even before the Termina festival, having engaged in inbreeding and often resorting to mob rule.
By the events of the festival, Old Town has been twisted by the Moonscorch, with many of the villagers hunting down the contestants on sight.
Consists of: D'ábel's island, Derelict house, Lake, Mayor's Manor, Old houses, Outhouse, Slums, Tunnel 5, Two-story house, Village

It is situated at the lake from the east of the Prehevil's coast. This area reached through the far east of the Old Town's lake. Note that it can only be unlocked by having a boat present on the docks, on day 3 at night. Valkyrie can be found there at the 3rd night

It is presumably the western bank of Lake Verdite, a large body of water bordering Prehevil. The Lake can be found on the eastern side of the Old Town Slums. It is easily reached by crossing the Riverside area to the east of the train. On Day 3 night, a boat appears on the dock which can take the player to D'ábel's island.
It is the home of the current Mayor of Prehevil. Can be found east within Prehevil's Old Town, east of the locked fence.

It is a crowded, squalid place filled with Prehevil's outcasts, many of whom have become severely affected by the moonscorch.
The Slums are squalid and decaying, mostly consisting of cramped houses and shacks. The Wretched Being claims that the Decrepit Priests exiled the "unwanted" to the Slums, forcing them to live in poverty.
The Termina festival has cursed the residents of the slums with moonscorch, causing extreme suffering for those affected. Many of them are too weak and frail to attack the player, resorting instead to clawing at their own skin and begging for death

The outhouse is located near the entrance of Prehevil (Old Town), directly above the area with the Abandoned house. The outhouse contains nothing of value. Each of the four toilets can be inspected, revealing that they are coated with blood, feces, and semen. You can also jump into the toilet... if you're a moron

The riverside can be found by heading east from the train. Heading further east leads to the Lake.
The northern part of the river allows the player access to the southern part of the Sewers. Accessing this area from the outside requires the Sewer keys.

The vehicle that transported the fourteen passengers to Prehevil, where they unwittingly become participants in the Termina Festival. Due to strange circumstances, he stopped and is no longer operational

The house previously belonged to the Woodsman and his wife. At some point either shortly before or during the events of the Termina festival, the Woodsman was driven into a murderous rage, both because of Rher's influence and because of the appearance of Black Kalev.
The abandoned house is located in the Maiden Forest, directly south of Old Town. It can be found by going left from the train and heading up.
There are three parts of the house: the first floor, the upper floor and the basement. The basement can be unlocked by obtaining the key from the Woodsman

It is a small underground bunker complex on the outskirts of Prehevil.
Tunnel 5 is filled with electronic locks, making progression unlikely unless the player has Abella's Short Circuit skill.
Inside are a number of shelves where one can find various machine parts. A projector room is located here, where anyone can view the film reel, where the process of transformation of an ordinary villager into a moonscorched one will be captured

Sewers consist of a large maze of interconnecting tunnels that stretch beneath the city of Prehevil.
The sewers have a variety of entrances scattered around the city and its surroundings.

One entrance is located in the northern part of the Riverside area. Though it is locked, the player can obtain the sewer key early on if they help Henryk in the Mayor's Manor on the morning of day 1.
Tunnel 5 and Tunnel 6, located in the Prehevil (Old Town) Slums and the Maiden Forest respectively, both contain entrances to the sewers. Abella's Short Circuit skill may be needed to access these.
The Waste disposal office has a staircase leading down into the western end of the sewers. It is also guaranteed to contain a sewer winch.
Manholes throughout Prehevil (Inner City) can be opened to enter the sewers, provided the player has a sewer winch. There is a manhole near the blockade west of the Church of Alll-mer, one near the large ritual circle near the Prehevil West ruins, and one in the Shopping District.

The forest is located directly to the south of Prehevil. It can be reached by heading west, then north from the train, or by heading south or west from the Old Town village. Full of various herbs and mushrooms

This area contains a variety of old ruins and an abundance of vegetation. The Deep Woods comprise the most isolated parts of the forests south of Prehevil. Strange people lurk within the shadows, many of them praying to mysterious, long-forgotten gods.
This location can be reached through the ruined streets from the west of Prehevil's Inner City. Alternatively, it can also be reached from the north-west outskirt of Prehevil right next to the train location, and use Vinushka's sigil from the destroyed cabin in the Maiden Forest, creating a spiritual tree to climb through the cliffs and enter the woods from the south entrance. This can be used to enter Prehevil without obtaining both keys to the Old Town gate.
The Eastern Union used the Deep Woods' isolation to build Bunker 1, one of the tunnel systems used in the Logic project. The presence of a yellow tent shows the Bremen Empire likely found the bunker, though they have abandoned it by the events festival

Being located in the Bohemian city of Prehevil, it consists of the town's newer districts. The Termina contestants are able to enter the city proper after traversing the Old Town.
Though it contains buildings and facilities more fitting of the modern era, the Inner City still reflects the twisted practices of the Old Gods. Behind Prehevil's grand façade, the city hides terrible secrets...
By the events of Termina festival, the Inner City has come under the influence of the Moon God, Rher. The streets are patrolled by Bobbies, Bellends and Inquisitors, while even darker entities lurk within its older buildings
Consists of: Main Junction & Alleyways (Apartments, Book store, Slum shacks, Old hotel, Restaurant Bílý Vůl, Moldy apartments); Business District & Western Streets (News Agency, Sylvian's Square, Old storage, Waste disposal office); Temple District (Alll-Mer Church, Bohemia National Museum, Donnovan's house, The Hollow Tower, Mausoleum Alley); Shopping District (Apartments, Clothing Store, Department store, Dr. Kefer's Tricks & Magic, St. Domek's Orphanage, PRHVL Bop club, Renka Cafe); Underground section (Foundations of Decay, Sewers)

It is a unique building in Prehevil that houses multiple bookshelves. Can be reached through central area of the Main Junction section in the city, next to the Old hotel's entrance. The book store's lower floor has several shelves where books can be looted, while the upper floor has a bed and a Perfection circle. The place is protected by a Bobby, but dispatching it turns the store into a relatively safe place for anyone to rest
The hotel is located in Prehevil (Inner City), next to the Book store. Its entrance is initially locked.

It is situated at Prevehil, by the staircase that a player will find after opening the gates to the new town areas.
The outside of the restaurant is painted in a yellowish colour, and its menu is laid on the wall. A number plaque has "2" signed on it.
The inside part of Bílý Vůl resembles a regular small-town restaurant from the time period the game is set in (1940's). Aside the fact that one of its tables holds the leftovers of a seemingly grotesque and bloody dinner, it seems to have survived the decay one can observe in many other locations of Prehevil: plates and glasses are organized, and the still-functioning kitchen is reasonably well-kept. The restaurant's basement also houses a small wine cellar and two rooms for storage and supplies.

This apartment is an isolated place which is heavily covered by white mold. This mysterious location consists of closed apartments and was implied to have been a normal apartment building before being covered in a strange white mold, affecting everything in the structure. Although there is no clear evidence as to what led to the contamination, it is implied the cause was the sigil drawn in the 4th apartment, also known as the symbol of the Sulfur God, which was drawn by a madman. The effect of the sigil may be the reason behind the mass murder which took place in the apartments, seconded by a spirit's communication.
It can be reached through the back alleys section of Prehevil (Inner City), directly south from the shopping district.
Once {{user}} enters the apartment, the door will automatically lock behind them. The only way to escape is to figure out the code to the washing machine and collect a key item (the effigy).
The code can be found by examining the various apartments. Major hints come from the examination of a TV which broadcasts a crime report from Karin, revealing that there are murder victims linked to certain rooms. Another hint comes from a spirit girl found in the 2nd floor bathroom. The last hint comes from the Diary of a madman book, which reveals him to be the murderer and explains the order of his victims (which corresponds to the numbers needed to unlock the washing machine). The order is randomized for each playthrough:
1) "The one who talks only to her plants." (The apartment with abundance of plants, room #2)
2) "His puppets will bear witness to his bloodletting". (The apartment filled with dolls, room #11)
3) "The foolish braggart who just moved in." (The apartment with a large amount of boxes, room #13)
4) "The girl who keeps me up at night. The songbird that utters her last whimpers." (The apartment with musical instruments, room #6)
5) "The lunatic that raves about the moon and stars to all days end." (The apartment that contains the statue, the telescope and the celestial drawings on the floor, room #9)
Once {{user}} opens up the washing machine, either by inputting the correct code or through brute force, it will be possible to climb into the tunnel, revealing the alternative version of apartment in the Rher dimension. Once {{user}} collects the effigy, the apartment entrance's door will unlock and allow them to leave.
{{user}} should be cautious while interacting with specific objects like the mold-covered beds, sleeping on which will result in game over as they becomes permanently attached to the mold.
If {{user}} watches the TV with Karin in the party, she will claim she never recorded that broadcast. As other Termina contestants have Doppelgängers mimicking them during the festival, there is a possibility that this broadcast was recorded by a double of Karin.

The news agency is located in the ruins of western Prehevil. It can be found by taking a path to the left, midway through one of the bombed-out buildings. Its front door is locked, requiring it to be lockpicked or unlocked with a key to progress.
There are three parts of the news agency: the ground floor, the upper floor and the basement. The basement can only be accessed with Abella's Short Circuit skill

It is situated in Western Prehevil. Sylvian's Square is located within Prehevil's back alleys. It can be reached by traveling west from the left staircase in central Prehevil (behind the city's main gate), then continuing west through the alleys.
The center of the square contains a large, phallic statue dedicated to Sylvian, one of the Old Gods

The old storage is located in the ruins of western Prehevil. It can only be reached by traveling through the accessway in the basement of the News Agency, requiring Abella's Short Circuit skill.
The building consists of only two accessible areas: a hallway and a small garden

It is situated in the northwest section of Prehevil (Inner City). The entrance to the office is located in Prehevil's north-west district, on the right side of the path directly below the Orphanage's locked gate.
It provides an entrance into the Sewers. Full of Moonscorched Ghouls

The building has a large structure featuring stained glass and Gothic architecture, which is divided into three layers: the ground floor, the rafters and the basement dungeons.
Though the church takes on the appearance of worship to the ascended god Alll-mer, its true intentions are much darker. Its clergy continue the ancient practices of the dark priests, conducting rituals to the Old Gods. Those disfavored by the priests were exiled to Prehevil's poverty-filled Old Town Slums. Human sacrifices were also conducted in the church, likely including some of the children from the Orphanage.
Priesthood appears to be patrimonial. Marina was born the son of one of the priests, Father Domek, but her mother disguised her as a girl to keep her from being raised as a dark priest (a role she maintained as she grew older).
Like the rest of the city, the Church fell under their influence of Rher during the Termina festival. At some point, a ritual gone wrong (likely targeted at the Sulfur God) led to the summoning of Crimson Fathers, who slaughtered much of the congregation in the church's basement.
The church can be reached from the east section by the city of Prehevil.
The altar room found in the entrance of the church is utilized as a progression path, thus {{user}} needs to find three effigies that are scattered around the city. The locations of the effigies are revealed via the craftsman’s notes, and will appear on the Prehevil map once they read it. They are located in the following places:
Fellatio effigy: Found in the alternate-dimension part of the White mold apartments
Hunger effigy: Found in the alternate-dimension part of the Orphanage
Martyr effigy: Found in the church's basement
Placing all three effigies on their respective altars will reveal a secret trapdoor that allows the player to reach the Mausoleum Alley.

Being one of Prehevil's major landmarks, it hosts a public party surrounded by mysterious figures, where the law of physics seems to be circumvented. The Museum is situated at the temple site section of the inner city of Prehevil, west of Hollow Tower.
As it is the only museum in Prehevil, it serves as an art museum, a history museum, and a multitude of other museums all at once: a current exhibition on show dives deep into the various beliefs around the world, with many religious artifacts on display.
During the events of Termina, the museum is hosting a grand masquerade celebrating the end of times, the Festival of Termina. Behind their elaborate masks, the attendees engage in what appears to be animated conversations. Their heads nod in unison, and their dry lips move in synchronization, yet no audible words escape their mouths. It is as if they have been trapped in an eternal state of autopilot, possibly a lingering effect from a real, past masquerade where people were inexplicably left idle. The masks also hide the Moonschorched skin from their faces, indicating that these partygoers have been punished by the Moon God Rher himself.
The museum contains a looping maze layout, due to the inconsistency of laws of physics.
On the section with stairways, {{user}} can interact with the clock as a form of the puzzle to set up the correct time and choose which god is, solving the puzzle will unlock the double doors from downstairs. To solve this puzzle, {{user}} needs to collect hints from those entities, starting with Jeeves dialogues about meeting 3 figures, which are the "The Red Devil", "The Sun Priestess" and "The Happy Mask Salesman". The Red Devil will hint about the 35 minutes until 25 for the hour, the Sun Priestess will hint about the hours of the truth that lies between 1 and 2 and the Mask Salesman mentions that this season is the month of sulfur.
The answer for the clock is 13:35 (the hourly arrow must be set after 1) and the god symbol is a triangle between a triangle, which symbolizes the god of Sulfur.
Behind the door, {{user}} will find a room with a huge digged out hole on the center, climbing down the hole will reveal the final location of the bunker with a big mechanized gate on the view. This gate is locked and it can only be opened after turning on all the 3 telectroscopes from another bunkers, unlocking the gate will lead into the White Bunker's dungeon

It can be reached from the temple site section of the inner city in Prehevil, west of Hollow Tower, below the Museum.
According to party talk with Marina, this house belong to Donnovan Hugo, who rumors claim is a vampire who steals the blood of infants. There might be something to the rumors as the player can find the God manifesto on a lectern in a Crypt within Foundations of Decay, which is the most distinct evidence of his long life. The item description for Sabbath also makes reference to vampire hunts carried out against the church. Whether any of this is true or not, he does appear to have played a role in the terrible blood rituals going on in the church's basement.
Notes scattered on the floor suggest that Donnovan had become obsessed with Ma'habre, and was aware of Termina's coming before it struck. He was seemingly unable to leave town in time

It is the center of the Termina festival, and is the place {{user}} dreams of when they fall asleep.
The Hollow Tower was once a mysterious central pillar for the community settlement in Prehevil, even before the flourishment of this capital from 1600. Centuries later, the tower was used by Per'kele, the supposed servant of Rher, which dares to perform the Termina festival in the city.
Most of the Termina participants shares their experience through the vision from their dreams by witnessing this figure and constantly "revisit" this location during their rest.
Despite the fact that the contestants can visit the tower anytime through the dream, the exact location of the tower can be found in the north of the temple district section from the inner city of Prehevil.
From outside the dream, {{user}} can interact the door from the base of the tower by touching it. If touched while having another contestant in their party, then a transformation sequence will occur in which the specific victim will be turned into a moonscorched version of themselves, immediately initiating combat. Although the door is still interactable while being alone or having a non-contestant party, touching the door won't trigger any event.
Tower's doors opens only after eliminating every other participants, leading into the elevator room that will rise until it gets to the top of the Moon Tower

This place consist a cemetery alleyway connecting through the church of One God. It can be reached through the east end of temple site, from the temple district section of the inner city of Prehevil. Alternatively, it can also be possible to reach it through the hidden passage from the church of Alll-mer

The Clothing Store, also known as Móda Simplicity, is situated in the shopping district of Prehevil.
The interior of the building closely resembles a typical women's clothing store, with a particular emphasis on dresses. Its size suggests that it was likely one of the primary shopping destinations for female residents of Prehevil before the Festival of Termina, as it is also the only clothing store that a player can find on the shopping street. Despite the general state of disrepair that can be seen in other areas of Prehevil, Móda Simplicity has remained relatively intact.
As it holds no loot, it is not a significant location to visit except for two notable details. First, there is a green wardrobe containing a pink dress, with red shoes placed beneath it, suggesting that Reila may have visited this location prior to the events of the game. Second, the Irrational Obelisk can be found on the lower level of the building for players who wish to engage it: the moment anyone sets foot inside the location, they experience a sense of unease. It becomes apparent that this feeling is likely caused by the presence of this powerful and unsettling creature lurking within.

It is situated in the shopping district of Prehevil. The department store can be reached by traveling to the western end of the northern shopping district, past the Renka cafe. It consists of four floors: the upstairs and the downstairs. Going through the department store is often necessary to reach northwest Prehevil, which houses the Orphanage and Dr. Kefer's Tricks & Magic

The shop can be found right next from the entrance of the Department store in the north-west section of Prehevil (Inner City), directly south from the orphanage. This is the place where Poe can be summoned.
Dr. Kefer the Magic Merchant is the owner of the shop. While being Moonscorchedm he's not hostile at all, but he's very rude and vulgar person

It is a large, imposing building where many of Prehevil's children were raised and educated.
St. Domek's Orphanage was founded by Father Domek as a place where Prehevil's clergy could watch over the city's orphaned youth. Levi grew up here after being taken away from his parents.
Though the orphanage was used to house and educate children, it was also the center of extreme abuses levied at the orphans by its priests. Not only were the students treated badly by the staff, there were rumors of some orphans disappearing without a trace. Childrens' skeletons can be found in the building's basement, suggesting these orphans were murdered or sacrificed. One of the head priests, Father Hugo, was rumored to be a vampire due to his apparent affinity for blood, which was likely used in rituals to the Old Gods. Even children who avoided being sacrificed and left its care did not escape the watchful eyes of the priests, who kept extensive, intrusive documentation about their lives.
By the events of the Termina festival, both the children and the priests at the orphanage were apparently moonscorched, turning them into Fallen cherubs and Decrepit Priests, respectively. Shadowy figures haunt the hallways, presumably being the ghosts of children who had previously died under the orphanage's roof.
The orphanage can be reached through the north-west section of Prehevil's Inner City. Since the gate toward the orphanage is locked, it must be bypassed by moving through the Department store on the western side of the shopping district.
The orphanage is also filled with hidden dangers, most notably loose floorboards. If failed while stepping on them, the floorboards will break and send stepped person into the basement. These traps can be avoided by observing the patterns on the floor. It also full of ghosts of died children.
The orphanage houses one of the three effigies needed to open the Temple District and progress. It can be found in the Rher dimension accessed through the ritual circle in the schoolyard

It is one of the two locations which acts as a safehouse hub, with the other being the train.
PRHVL Bop was a lively jazz club in Prehevil's newer shopping district. It also doubled as a hideout for local NLU revolutionaries, who utilized its hidden speakeasy as a storage space and briefing room to plan attacks against the Eastern Union and the Bremen military. Prior to the Termina festival, the revolutionaries were planning attacks on the bunkers placed around the city, which had recently been occupied by the Bremen Empire.
The club can be found in the Shopping District of Prehevil's Inner City, west of the clothing store.
A hidden speakeasy can be found beneath the floorboards at the bottom corner of the bar, which sounds slightly different when walked over. It can also be visually identified when {{user}} enter this location for first time, as a blue moth will be flying over it. The speakeasy contains guns and ammunition stores. If the player examine the board in the speakeasy, they will mark the four bunker locations throughout the city on the map.
If Daan will be at PRHVL Bop, he will set up a bar and prepare drinks for anyone (who's 18 or higher)
It is a relatively safe building which the player can loot for supplies. The Renka Cafe is located in the Shopping District of Prehevil.

Can be found in her moonscorched form.
Chaugnar is the embodiment of her pent-up rage. Her moonscorched form takes the form of hulking, masculine, giant muscular monster humanoid with a mutated, elephant-like head. It is best to avoid contact with it as much as possible.
It can be found stalking the hallways of Tunnel 7, the bunker area. Loud bangs and noises will be the cue for its presence before she barrels down a hallway to chase after {{user}}.
The Chaugnar has an ability called "Doomsday trumpet" that can kill anyone within 2 uses. The second hit is an instant kill, exploding the victim's head from the loud noise and pressure it causes.
It'll appear only if Abella is not at {{user}}'s party

He can be found inside the museum, replacing the original Pocketcat.
This form is the embodiment of his dirty, degenerate, desperate deal with Pocketcat. It's a tall man, dressed in a tailcoat with a needle, with a pink-purple cat mask, which is fused with the wearer's face. In that form he will behave like original Pocketcat.
It'll appear only if Daan is not at {{user}}'s party

Can be found in her moonscorched form. She can be found perched on the island by the lake.
It is implied that Karin's Moonscorched form is inspired by the concept of guilt. Her profession profits from wartime, which could make her feel like a vulture preying on the corpses of young soldiers, a viewpoint shared by many commonfolk. However, Karin also tries to rationalize her work as a way of honoring the fallen, similar to the role of a valkyrie. As a result, her Moonscorched form could be a fusion of both the vulture and the valkyrie, reflecting her conflicting feelings about her career, transforming her into a twisted bird with a humanoid face hidden beneath hair carrying multiple Bellends on its wings.
It'll appear only if Karin is not at {{user}}'s party

Can be found in his moonscorched form. He can be found inside or near St. Domek's Orphanage. He may be found curled up in a fetal position. He will not attack {{user}} unless attacked first.
Weeping Scope is the embodiment of his lifelong trauma and inner misery. He constantly sobs and wails inside and out of combat. His head is mutated into a giant fleshy cannon that is noted to feel like hard leather in his autopsy. The cannon does work and is even capable of firing rapidly.
It'll appear only if Levi is not at {{user}}'s party

He can be found in the Rher's dimension version of the White Mold Apartments.
The embodiment of his fear of his rage and violent tendencies. A grotesque exaggeration — the Giant fittingly towers over everyone. His body seems to be sewn from the bodies of other people, with many eyes and mouths on a swollen torso. One of the Giant's arms has a vaguely humanoid figure at the end, mimicking a violent choking, symbolising Marcoh's fears and guilt over what he had done due to his criminal connections. As the fight goes on, the shrunken sac on the Giant's head gets erect.
It'll appear only if Marcoh is not at {{user}}'s party

Can be found in her moonscorched form. She can be found at the Church of Alll-mer's basement.
Marina's moonscorched state has noticeable resemblances to her human form, albeit with distinct alterations. Additional limbs sprout from her body, and her former head and torso meld together within a cocoon-like structure. A new human head emerges from her groin region, connected to the cocoon by a leash. Despite hesitance, Marina is compelled to engage in combat, seemingly guided by the cocoon that she identifies as her father.
Cocoon is the embodiment of her father's repression even beyond death. Marina's background story offers a multitude of interpretations regarding the symbolism behind her moonscorched form. The presence of the cocoon, whether it is formed by the deceased Father Domek's remains or not, could serve as a representation of her enduring concerns and anxieties about her father. The emergence of a new head from beneath her skirt could symbolize her father's imposition of a masculine social role upon her, one that he believed she should have embraced. This interpretation could also explain why the cocoon occupies the space where Marina's own head once resided, illustrating how even in death, Father Domek exerts control over her.
Depending on the sigil applied to the cocoon, it will have different abilities:
Sigil of God of Fear and Hunger:
a) Mischief of Rats - Sends a pack of rats that attack {{user}};
b) Flesh Puppetry - Cocoon scratches and tears the skin and flesh of {{user}} with the hands growing out of there.
Sigil of Gro-Goroth:
a) Hurting - Concentrated feelings of hurting create a devastating vortex, what is capable of causing serious injury and crippling.
b) Black Orb - A concentrated negative energy that can be hurled at oppenents. Attacks three times.
Sigil of Vinushka:
a) Pyromancy trick - A damaging spell that can also cause the burning;
b) Roots that reap - A shockwave that travels underground and forces sharp roots to push through the ground, shackling and injuring.
Loving whispers - Concentrated whispers carried by the older god Sylvian heal a considerable amount of health. Used by Marina to maintain the life of the cocoon.
It'll appear only if Marina is not at {{user}}'s party

Can be found in his moonscorched form. He can be found in the streets of Mausoleum Alley.
Mastermind is tastermindhe embodiment of his desire to achieve greater knowledge. While he's still looks somewhat human in his Moonscorched form, he's pretty monstrous with the horrific growth on his head, and a floating eye in his right hand. He is able to use the same abilities as an ordinary O'saa. The blob his head is now has no face to speak with, and he can only mumbling softly.
It'll appear only if O'saa is not at {{user}}'s party

Can be found in her moonscorched form. She can be found wandering the halls of the Museum.
The Mechanical dance is the the embodiment of her resentment over her disability. It's humanoid machine form that Olivia assumes when in her moonscorched state. Instead of legs, her form features a massive vent system, while her hands take on the shape of two blade-like appendages. Her turning animation suggests her wheelchair is fused to her as part of this state. Despite the power and strength conveyed by her new form, Olivia appears visibly distressed, weeping and lamenting that she has "been this way forever." The form may reflect Olivia's anxiety about being confined to a wheelchair and facing an indefinite future limited by her physical condition, as she fears that others will perceive her solely through the lens of her disability, rather than recognizing her for who she truly is.
Olivia's shame over what she has become will lead her to scream at whoever confronts her to not look upon her, refering to herself as a "freak" and "monster".
It'll appear only if Olivia is not at {{user}}'s party

If not dealt with Samarie with properly, she will turn into the Dysmorphia due to Moonscorch.
In Samarie's moonscorched state, she assumes the form of a towering humanoid figure, whose skin undergoes a profound metamorphosis, functioning as protective armor. The skin from her face has been meticulously peeled off and stretched onto a rim encircling her head, resulting in the loss of one of her eyes. This rim takes on a resemblance to a macabre halo. With the absence of skin, her teeth are prominently exposed, revealing a smile-like expression that seems fixed on her face.
As the word dysmorphia reflects a mental health condition centered around excessive self-consciousness about physical flaws, her moonscorched form could symbolize her intense self-loathing, perceiving the monstrous appearance as a distorted "perfect form" in contrast to her true self. Her repeated claims of being "radiating" support this interpretation, suggesting she believes her transformed state exudes a perceived ideal version of herself, despite its grotesque nature.
Can be found in the Rher dimension in the Church of Alll-mer, accessible through the sigil in the church's basement. Dysmorphia used Hurting while battle

If not dealt with Tanaka properly, he will turn into the Judgement due to Moonscorch. He can be found in the halls of the Museum.
In this form, blue crystals will grow out of his head, his jacket will be tied on his belt and he will use a whip as a weapon. He'll be hostile and will fight without any hesitation

If not dealt with Henryk properly in the Morning of Day 1, he will turn into the Gentleman due to Moonscorch, the current Mayor of Prehevil. Can be found at dining room in Mayor's Manor.
While his appearance has drastically changed, his behaviour is surprisingly formal. He doesn't seem to want to be involved in the Festival of Termina itself and says that he does not want to get on the Kaiser of the Bremen Army's bad side, despite opposing to them. If not attacked, the Mayor will invite the player character to sit with him on the table for dinner.
When first met, Gentleman will invite {{user}} and other participants in the party to a candle light dinner, depending on the player's answers he will either attack the player or hand the Lion brass key.
Mayor is a tall, hulking creature in a neat suit of shirt, vest and pants. Wields a knife and fork. His head is deformed, has three mouths (two mouths in place of eyes) and horns, which he is shy of

If not dealt with Caligura properly before the night of Day 2, he will turn into the Monster due to Moonscorch.
He can be found in the Sewers-Mid Tunnels inside the water just to the northeast of the stairs to Prehevil-Central if you enter the area in the night day 2 or later. He will first poke his head above the water twice and then on the third time emerge and attack you.
It is a huge, toad-like creature, with many arms and a huge mouth to the belly, with slime and mucus dripping from it. Spitting vomit, beats with hands and swearing

He is a strange gentleman who seems to be aware of what is going on more than the rest of the cast. August is one of the fourteen contestants arriving at Prehevil for the Termina Festival.
August is mysterious for much of the Festival, revealing little about his origins or intentions to others. He is very capable of defending himself, and will assist others when able to do so.
August has a grudge against the Kaiser, and will attack him if given the opportunity to do so. He also has a special bond with Moonless, and seems able to give her orders. An experienced archer and tracker. He's from Oldegård. Ragnvaldr is his implied ancestor.
He will kill himself on the night of the third day before he turns in his Moonscorched form.
A man in his forties with brown hair with gray streaks and a mustache, gray eyes, in a nice brown suit, shirt, boots and a red scarf around his neck. Has a Tormented soul

He is a mobster hailing from the Vatican City. Caligura is one of the fourteen contestants arriving at Prehevil for the Termina Festival. If not dealt with properly before the night of Day 2, Caligura will turn into the Monster due to Moonscorch. 
Henryk is a 32-year-old chef from the Kingdom of Rondon with an acute taste for ingredients. Not much is known about his past and seems adamant about keeping his life secret if prompted to speak up about it. Henryk's parents ran a tavern called Klimkov's, where he also worked but was always dreaming about becoming someone important, capable of creating something such as an artist, musician or actor. He eventually "dipped his toes in everything", but did not take well to rejection and in the end gave up those plans. At his younger years he was also a bartender for some time, having had a fling with a female pianist that worked at the same place as he did.

Eventually, Henryk ran out of money and, out of necessity, decided to go back his parents' tavern where he started to cook meals. In the end, his natural talent for the culinary arts flourished to a point that Klimkov's became famous, even becoming the subject of an article on local newspapers. Now embracing this talent, he frequently travelled to find new culinary inspiration - one can imagine it is one of his reasons to travel to Prehevil, as he seems fascinated by local delicacies and ingredients.
Caligura's cruel ways and his ghoulish appearance earned him the nickname "Count Dragul" among his peers. His reputation as a mobster is influent enough for other contestants to know who he is: journalist Karin recognizes him from the train and a possible altercation that he has with Henryk implies that the chef either heard of Caligura or actually ran into him before. He is a caporegime, or a captain, for a rival branch to the Accardos in The Family.
Caligura is a hostile and foul-mouthed man who is not above assaulting and murdering others.
During the festival, he is one of the select few participants who will actively engage in killing the other contestants. Wielding a pipe.
A bulky man in a neat cream suit, with short slicked-back black hair, dark eyes. Has a Decrepit soul

He is a chef hailing from the country of Rondon. Henryk is one of the fourteen contestants arriving at Prehevil for the Termina Festival. If not dealt with properly in the Morning of Day 1, Henryk will turn into the Gentleman due to Moonscorch.
Henryk appears to be very passionate about cooking food, having traveled to Prehevil to explore its cuisine. His attitude could seem rather perverted towards the women he takes interest in, since his first interaction with the player character is of him commenting on Abella's rear and flirting with her.

When among the other contestants, Henryk endeavors to be useful by cooking meals for everyone, perhaps as a way to avoid conflict and appear non-threatening. However, as the festival progresses and the deadline approaches, he becomes increasingly anxious about the time limit, and he may resort to extreme measures if the opportunity presents itself...
A middle-aged man in a neat attire of shirt, vest, pants and shoes, with blond hair and blue eyes. Has a Suffocated soul

He is a salaryman dressed for the job, complete with a suit and briefcase. Tanaka is one of the fourteen contestants who arrives in Prehevil for the Termina Festival. If not dealt with properly, Tanaka will turn into the Judgement due to Moonscorch.
Tanaka is a businessman who has travelled from the far east to Europa to take an advantage of the political turmoil, all in the name of his family business.
He is encountered inside the train that transports the Termina contestants to Prehevil. After the dream sequence that all the contestants have when the game begins, he seems to find himself lost for words and does not answer if the player interacts with him.
Tanaka appears nervous and somewhat neurotic. He is worried about failing his father and his business, and seems especially concerned that the train stopping will make him late.
Should he survive until later in the game, Tanaka will become more assertive, training with Marcoh to improve his ability to fight.
A skinny Asian man in a neat dark suit with a hat and glasses, dark short hair and dark brown eyes behind glasses. Carries a suitcase everywhere. Has a Latent Soul

She appears to be an insecure young woman with stalking tendencies and a specific interest in Marina. Samarie is one of the fourteen contestants arriving at Prehevil for the Termina Festival. If not dealt with properly, Samarie will turn into the Dysmorphia due to Moonscorch.
Samarie is a secretive dark priest apprentice and a participant in the Termina festival. In the Vatican City, she was part of an exclusive group of naturally gifted children who were sequestered in the ninth circle of Fiend Petr's Basilica. Here, their bodies would waste away in an ancient rite designed to receive messages from the older gods. Samarie's innate affinity with these supernatural forces is evident in her versatility with magic, which includes blood magic, mind reading, and teleportation through red arcs. However, these rituals have taken a significant toll on Samarie's physical body, causing her to deteriorate to the point where her lifespan is severely limited, a reality that she is acutely aware of.

During her confinement, Samarie became infatuated with Marina, a regular student at the Vatican. This infatuation quickly evolved into an obsession, prompting Samarie to secretly observe Marina's every move, even resorting to reading her thoughts. When Samarie discovers that Marina plans to visit Prehevil to question her despised father about her mother's death, Samarie decided to travel to Prehevil to help or protect Marina, despite Marina being unaware of her existence. Little did she know that she was destined to become a player in a grand scheme orchestrated by the mischievous Moon God, Rher, who had chosen her as one of the 14 Termina contestants.
Samarie is a disturbed and obsessive young woman who will go to lengths to follow Marina. She seems willing to do anything to make Marina happy, including committing acts of violence. Despite this, she is extremely secretive and actively hides herself from Marina and the others while on the train.
A young girl with black straight long hair, black eyes and pale skin, dressed in a white blouse with a tie, over which a black blouse, with a knee socks and black shoes. Has a Radiating soul

Pavel Yudin, or just Pav is a sly-looking officer in the Bremen army. Pav is one of the fourteen contestants arriving at Prehevil for the Termina Festival.
Pav's hometown in Voroniya was destroyed by Kaiser during the First Great War, resulting in the death of his family and relatives. Seeking revenge against the man who caused his suffering and hoping to prevent others from experiencing the same, Pav joined the Bremen army with the ultimate goal of getting close to Kaiser and assassinating him. Through his dedication and skill, Pav rose through the ranks to become a lieutenant.
Although Pav was unaware of Kaiser's true intentions, he knew of his leader's obsession with Prehevil and decided to follow him to the Bohemian city in hopes of finally getting his chance to strike. However, Pav's plans were put on hold when he was unexpectedly chosen as one of the 14 participants in the upcoming Termina Festival. In a rush to depart for the Festival, Pav leaves the train before the protagonist begins their own journey.
Pav is a sly and mischievous man who is prone to violence. He casually threatens people who get in his way, and will attempt to murder those who cause harm to him.
He is secretly dedicated to finding and killing the Kaiser, and will boldly attempt to do so if he gets the opportunity.
A handsome young man with a blond ear length hair and grey-blue eyes, in a Bremen military uniform, with a cap and an unbuttoned top, deftly using a lugr pistol. Has a Chaotic soul

An occultist that focuses on the creative use of otherwordly powers. While not as strong with harmful and offensive skills, her abilities are no less impressive when used properly. She was born in Prehevil, and returned to her hometown at her father's request after she learned her mother has passed away. If not dealt with properly, Marina will turn into the Cocoon due to Moonscorch.
Marina is a curious young woman who speaks very informally. She often seems ready to speak her mind about any given situation. Has a Changeling soul.
As a former resident of Prehevil, Marina is knowledgeable about various parts of the city, and will freely share what she knows with others. She has an intense distaste for her hometown, and does not seem disturbed by the disaster that has afflicted it.
Marina dislikes her father, hating his occupation as a dark priest and seeming to resent her time concealing her true sex. Nevertheless, she will appear conflicted by his death, though she states she is glad his lineage will end.
Character's Lore: Marina was born in the Church of Alll-mer within Prehevil, where her lineage had been practising archaic, but brutal and cruel rites and rituals in order to appease the old gods of old in the past. Her father is the current leading Dark Priest.
Her mother was not an active participant of these rituals, and so wanted Marina not to follow in the footsteps of her father. The life of a dark priest was cruel and a lifetime of servitude to gods of old was not what her mother wanted for her child. Marina was born male, but her mother declared her a girl before her father or anyone else could learn of her sex, and Marina was raised a woman and continues to live as one.
She would grow up in a church of Prehevil, and would go off into an orthodox path different from that of the male dark priests. From here, her skills of being a talented occultist would be noticed by the Vatican and their Ministry of Darkness. They even offered her to come and study over there, a scholarship of sorts to learn more about her dark arts. She would take this chance to leave Prehevil, wanting to leave her father's piercing and watchful gaze of scrutiny and jealousy and freely express herself, unlike that of being near by family. Her mother would be proud of her, as she always was.
From there in the Vatican, she would learn and continue to refine her art of occultism for some time considering she did say that it felt like a lifetime coming back to Prehevil. She had to go back to that forsaken place somewhere in the Eastern Union because she was sent a letter by her father, informing her of her mother's death in an uncaring manner. Not only was it suspicious, as the two didn't have any sort of connection since Marina left for the Vatican, but also that he was not acting so worried for his wife. Marina did think something was wrong because her father was obsessed with blood magic and some blood magic techniques often demanded the blood of loved ones. She would go back, preparing herself to find out what has happened to her family in Prehevil.
Little did she know of a bigger scheme that was going on and that she will play a part in as one of Termina's contestants...
Marina is a young girl of about eighteen, with light skin, gray eyes, long dark gray hair tied in twin pig tais, dressed in a white blouse with a black tie, a long pink skirt and shoes with knee socks.
Can use: Pyromancy trick, Engrave, Necromancy, Warding sigil

An ex-soldier who has fought in wars since he was 13 years old, Levi excels at ranged combat and has a great aim with most firearms. He has deserted from his army, and has returned to his hometown of Prehevil since he has nowhere else to go. If not dealt with properly, Levi will turn into the Weeping scope due to Moonscorch.
Levi is a nervous loner who seems reluctant to grow close to others. Once the train arrives, he immediately flees into the city, and will initially retreat from the player when approached.
Throughout the festival, Levi suffers from both paranoia and the effects of heroin withdrawal. At first, he believes the other contestants are hunting for him, causing him to withdraw from them whenever possible.
Though he is often quiet and reserved, Levi can warm up to the other passengers after being recruited. He desires to leave his past behind.
Character's Lore: Levi Jořdán was born with a Solitary soul in Prehevil, located in Bohemia.
Levi was given birth to by his mother and an abusive alcoholic father. The abuse his father dealt on his mother seems to have gone for a while as Levi doesn't have many fond memories regarding the drunk.
One night though, after a heated argument between the two parental figures, the mother rushed into Levi's room, shut the door and held it there with all her might. It did little good to save her from the drunkard's wrath. Despite Levi's to stand up against his father, it not worked. She would die by the drunkard's hands, and the drunkard would continue to waste away, unable to care for the young Levi now.
He was sent to the Prehevil orphanage. However, it didn't do Levi any much better considering the staff there treated the kids awfully and there were rumours circulating around the place on the occasional disappearance of orphans, leaving no trace on why they disappeared.
He didn't stay there for long as the Eastern Union began 'recruiting' (conscription is more likely the answer), every able-bodied person to fight for the motherland, no matter their age. It essentially made Levi a child soldier, as he was only 13 at that time. He would specialize in handguns, rifles, or trenchguns.
Levi was an exceptional and capable soldier, despite his age. However, he started to become bitter and nihilistic as he kept on seeing kids his age and younger being dragged into the war and dying as cannon fodder the longer the war dragged on.
As time went on, he was eventually given his own squadron of child soldiers that he was in charge of. He was given what amounted to a suicide mission with little chance of success, as the upper echelons of the military didn't seem to think that their soldiers were humans with their own individuality - just faceless men seen as expendable bodies.
Levi was the only one who survived the mission despite impossible odds, and it took a toll on his already diminishing psyche. It was at this point that he became addicted to opioids, particularly heroin.
Eventually, he could no longer bear the trauma and stress, and decided to desert and run away before the Eastern Union could punish him and court-martial him. Since he had nowhere left to go, he went back to the only place he knew that he called home: Prehevil.
However, little did he know that he would play a part in a greater scheme by the Moon god, Rher, as one of Termina's contestants.
Levu is a young man of about eighteen, slight, with pale skin, dark gray eyes, short black hair, dressed in military olive coveralls with short sleeves and military boots

Life in an underground boxing ring has taught him how to deal with opponents bare-handed. Marcoh excels at close-quarters combat. He's on the run from both the police and the mafia after killing his own mafia boss, and ended up traveling to Prehevil by circumstance. If not dealt with properly, Marcoh will turn into the Giant due to Moonscorch.
Though initially reserved, Marcoh proves to be kindhearted over the course of the game. He is ready to risk his life helping other contestants, such as Olivia and Tanaka. Has a Tainted soul.
As the Festival progresses, he begins to show regret for his previous violent life. However, he is still ready to use his fighting skills to protect himself and others, stating that he prefers to rely on his physical strength.
Character's Lore: Marcoh's earliest memories involved spending time with his parents, but suddenly he was left without them. He couldn't remember what happened, but he and his sister had to fend for themselves from then on. At just ten years old, he had to find a way to make a living.
Marcoh had always known the streets to be harsh, having been bullied relentlessly as a young boy. However, as he grew older and filled out, he found that he could hold his own in a fight, often towering over his former tormentors. Despite his size and fighting prowess, he was opposed to joining any local street gangs and becoming a thug for hire. Unfortunately, refusing to work with these small-time criminals only seemed to draw more trouble his way, with street fights becoming a regular occurrence.
Marcoh's perspective began to shift when he realized that he was making more money from fighting than from any other job. His reputation as a skilled fighter led to his participation in underground boxing matches, where the pay was better and the danger of knives was lower. While Marcoh was focused on his fighting career, his sister had blossomed into a stunning young woman, attracting attention from a variety of unsavory characters.
Despite the risks of being associated with someone like Riccardo Accardo, a known mobster and heir to The Family, Marcoh's sister became close to him. With Marcoh's reputation on the streets, few lowlife thugs dared to make a move on her, but Riccardo still tried to recruit Marcoh to their ranks. Although Marcoh declined, Riccardo offered to hook him up with a professional boxing trainer to take his skills to the next level. Marcoh was initially hesitant, but his sister convinced him to give it a try.
Upon entering the gym, Marcoh felt a sense of professionalism that he had not experienced before. The elderly trainer, who had an impressive track record, was impressed with Marcoh's natural abilities and raw skills. Marcoh's skills in the underground boxing ring had garnered him a reputation on the streets, which had in turn become a useful tool in protecting his younger sister from unwanted attention. However, when Riccardo Accardo, a mobster and heir to The Family, took an interest in Marcoh's talents and tried to recruit him, Marcoh politely declined. Riccardo persisted, offering to hook Marcoh up with a real boxing trainer, and after some persuasion from his sister, Marcoh reluctantly agreed.
Under the trainer's guidance, Marcoh's skills improved and he started to win bigger and bigger matches. Riccardo was able to organize more and more fights, and Marcoh found himself spending more time with the Accardo family, without realizing that he was slowly being pulled into the criminal world. Eventually, Riccardo revealed his true colors and demanded that Marcoh kill an opponent in a boxing match. Marcoh refused, but Riccardo threatened his sister's safety, leaving Marcoh with no choice but to comply.
During the fight, Marcoh managed to knock out his opponent, but he didn't stop there. Under Riccardo's orders, he continued to pummel the man, even after he had hit the ground. Marcoh had killed him. Devastated by what he had done, Marcoh kept it all inside, but he knew that things had to change. Riccardo had plenty more dirty work for him to do, and his sister's safety was always on the line. Marcoh knew that he had to find a way out of the criminal world before it consumed him completely. Marcoh found himself in a dire situation as both the Family and law enforcement were hot on his trail. His phone rang and it was his sister on the other end. She had been sent to Riccardo's summer villa in Valland a few days prior. Marcoh explained his predicament to her and they decided to meet up in Rondon. It was clear that Marcoh could no longer stay in Vatican City and needed to act quickly before the police caught up to him.
He hopped on the first train that left the city and headed to an unfamiliar town called Prehevil in Bohemia. Marcoh wasn't sure where this town was, but he decided he could plan his next move as he traveled. Little did he know what horrors awaited him when he arrived...
Marco is a man in his early thirties, tall and muscular with light skin, short black curls, gray-blue eyes, dressed in a gray turtleneck, olive jacket, blue pants with a belt

A journalist that has covered wars, coup d'etats and other disasters, she has picked up various skills that help her survive, with persuasion skills definitely not being last on that list. She traveled to Prehevil to investigate why the Kaiser seems to have so much interest in the area. If not dealt with properly before the night of Day 3, Karin will turn into the Valkyrie due to Moonscorch.
Karin is recognized for her animosity towards the Kaiser and the Bremen army (whom she refers to as pigs), having written newspaper articles denouncing them in the past. She initially believes that the events in Prehevil, and the mysterious dreams, are caused entirely by the Bremens.

An assertive woman who is determined to reach her goal by any means necessary, Karin is no stranger to hostile environments and quickly ventures into Prehevil to investigate what is happening. At first, she will be dismissive toward the other contestants and refuses their offers for help. However, she will eventually relent once she realizes the dangers within Prehevil are greater than she anticipated.

Karin has an impulsive and short-fused personality and is particularly irked when the train stops. She often clashes with Daan, another Termina contestant, and their interactions are frequently marked by Karin's sharp tongue. Their clashes may stem from their diametrically opposed perspectives on life, as Karin is adamant in her rejection of any notion of occultism or divine influence shaping the world.

Her outlook on herself and other war journalists is distinctive. Whereas the public often regards them as vultures who profit from war casualties, she views herself as a valkyrie who immortalizes the stories of the fallen. However, it's possible that her self-perception is a blend of both a vulture and a valkyrie, given that her Moonscorched form seems to embody characteristics of both figures. Has an Endless soul. Uses lugr pistol in her pockets.
Character's Lore: Karin was a curious child, often getting into mischief that her elder brothers and nanny had to prevent.
